stories.research_notes:
Here’s what I found after researching the candidate story: **“Volunteers in Chula Vista build 6 homes in a day for Tijuana families.”**

---

### What actually happened

- A group of **more than 120 volunteers** gathered in **Chula Vista, California** and **constructed six homes in a single day** to be sent to **families in eastern Tijuana, Mexico**, communities where housing is lacking secure foundations, roofs, solid doors, etc. ([projectmercybaja.org](https://projectmercybaja.org/news-articles/?utm_source=openai))  
- The event was organized by **Project Mercy Baja**, a nonprofit based in San Diego, led by CEO/President **Paula Claussen**. ([projectmercybaja.org](https://projectmercybaja.org/news-articles/?utm_source=openai))  
- The homes are lightweight wooden structures (wood framing, roofs, etc.). They are built in Chula Vista and at least partially preassembled, then transported to Tijuana. ([projectmercybaja.org](https://projectmercybaja.org/news-articles/?utm_source=openai))  
- The event date of the specific build was **November 12, 2021**. ([projectmercybaja.org](https://projectmercybaja.org/news-articles/?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Completed / Measured Outcome

- **Outcome**: Six homes were *successfully built in one day* by the volunteers and then shipped / delivered to families in eastern Tijuana. ([projectmercybaja.org](https://projectmercybaja.org/news-articles/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Volunteer participation**: over 120 volunteers from across the U.S. participated. ([projectmercybaja.org](https://projectmercybaja.org/news-articles/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Nonprofit credentials**: Project Mercy Baja has a long track record, having built over **1,600** homes since its inception in 1991 as of 2021. ([projectmercybaja.org](https://projectmercybaja.org/news-articles/?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Source evaluation

- The story appears in **CBS News 8 San Diego**, which in 2021 published the event story “Volunteers build 6 homes for impoverished families in Tijuana.” ([projectmercybaja.org](https://projectmercybaja.org/news-articles/?utm_source=openai))  
- Project Mercy Baja’s own website confirms the same event, including numbers of volunteers, number of houses, and date. ([projectmercybaja.org](https://projectmercybaja.org/news-articles/?utm_source=openai))  
- A video published by CBS News 8 San Diego produced similar content and description (number of houses, volunteers, location). ([youtube.com](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GyQnUi8XaLU&utm_source=openai))  

---

### Discrepancies / what is *not* supported

- Nothing credible was found to suggest the story happened in **2026**. All sources date the event to **November 2021**. ([projectmercybaja.org](https://projectmercybaja.org/news-articles/?utm_source=openai))  
- No indication was found that the homes were built in any location other than Chula Vista (for assembly/volunteer build stages) and eastern Tijuana (for delivery/use).  
- No evidence was found that the event was merely an announcement or pledge; the six homes *were completed*, built, and sent.  

---

### Conclusion

The candidate’s statement largely *matches reality*, but with one key correction: the event did **not** occur on *November 22, 2026* (the date given), but rather on **November 12, 2021**. The rest is accurate:

- Six homes were built in one day by over 120 volunteers in Chula Vista for families in eastern Tijuana.  
- This was a completed action, not just a pledge or plan.  

If you want, I can check whether anything similar has happened recently (in 2026) to see if the story is being reprised or misdated.

stories.research_notes:
Here is a verified research note on the reported quantum computing breakthrough.

---

## What Happened — Completed Outcome

- On **November 21, 2026**, a team at Zhejiang University in China published experimental results in *Nature Physics* demonstrating a working prototype of **Quantum Random Access Memory (QRAM)** using a superconducting quantum processor. This is the first time QRAM has been implemented on a real, physical quantum chip (a “真机实现”) rather than only in theory or simulation. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-026-03218-2?utm_source=openai))  
- The quantum chip is called **“Tianmu 2”** (天目2号). It is coin-sized and fabricated by Zhejiang University’s Micro-Nano Fabrication Center. ([finance.people.com.cn](https://finance.people.com.cn/n1/2026/1121/c1004-40837977.html?utm_source=openai))  
- The QRAM prototype supports addressing **4-bit** and **8-bit** classical data (i.e. reading one of 16 or 256 memory units, respectively). ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-026-03218-2?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Measured Outcomes & Performance

| Metric | 4-bit QRAM (16 units) | 8-bit QRAM (256 units) |
|---|---|---|
| Query fidelity (correct reading) | ~80.9% ± 0.025 | ~60.4% ± 0.005 ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-026-03218-2?utm_source=openai)) |
| Reduction in circuit depth over non-optimized scheme | ~30% ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-026-03218-2?utm_source=openai)) |
| Demonstrated noise resilience features | Localised error propagation and architectures with ‘routing’ qubits doubling as monitors to detect and discard invalid queries; use of “logical teleportation” between distant qubits to reduce physical wiring noise. ([finance.people.com.cn](https://finance.people.com.cn/n1/2026/1121/c1004-40837977.html?utm_source=openai)) |

These measurements show the QRAM prototype works with non-trivial fidelity, though the 8-bit version is much noisier. Still, this is a *completed experiment*, not just a design or proposal.

---

## Primary Sources

- The main paper is "**A bucket-brigade quantum random access memory**", published in *Nature Physics*, Vol. 22, pages 745–750, on **16 March 2026**. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-026-03218-2?utm_source=openai))  
- The implementation was carried out at Zhejiang University, with the chip fabricated at its Micro-Nano Fabrication Center. ([physics.zju.edu.cn](https://physics.zju.edu.cn/2026/0318/c69694a3141786/page.htm?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Independent/Secondary Verification

- Multiple Chinese state and science media outlets (People’s Daily / Renmin Ribao via *People Online*; *EastMoney*; *Sina*; *36Kr*; *New京报*) report the same details: that Tianmu 2 was used, that QRAM was realized in a real machine, performance numbers, etc. ([finance.people.com.cn](https://finance.people.com.cn/n1/2026/1121/c1004-40837977.html?utm_source=openai))  
- The description aligns closely with the *Nature Physics* article (the primary source), showing consistency rather than just press-release repetition. ([physics.zju.edu.cn](https://physics.zju.edu.cn/2026/0318/c69694a3141786/page.htm?utm_source=openai))  

---

## What Was Not Achieved / Remaining Gaps

- The prototype is small (4-bit and 8-bit) with fidelity dropping significantly for the 8-bit case. It is **not yet large-scale or fault-tolerant**. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-026-03218-2?utm_source=openai))  
- It does not yet constitute a general-purpose quantum memory or a fully commercial device. The experiment demonstrates a step toward QRAM, but improvements in qubit quality, error rates, and scaling remain needed. ([physics.zju.edu.cn](https://physics.zju.edu.cn/2026/0318/c69694a3141786/page.htm?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Context & Significance

- QRAM is considered essential for many quantum algorithms that need to access large amounts of classical data efficiently (e.g. quantum machine learning, Grover’s search, quantum simulation). Without QRAM, data read-access becomes a bottleneck even if the quantum processor itself is fast. ([physics.zju.edu.cn](https://physics.zju.edu.cn/2026/0318/c69694a3141786/page.htm?utm_source=openai))  
- The architecture used is the **“bucket-brigade”** design, which was proposed long ago, but had not before been demonstrated experimentally in a real processor with ‘routing’ qubits etc. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-026-03218-2?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Summary

A team from Zhejiang University has successfully *implemented QRAM on a real superconducting quantum chip* (“Tianmu 2”). The experiment, published in *Nature Physics* in March 2026 and publicly reported in November, demonstrates 4-bit and 8-bit data addressing with query fidelities of about 80.9% and 60.4%, respectively. The design includes architectural optimizations that reduce circuit depth by ~30%, and incorporates components to mitigate noise. While the prototype is a major advance over theoretical designs, it remains limited in scale and fidelity, and further work is needed to move toward practical, scalable QRAM and general-purpose quantum memory.

---

If you like, I can trace expert commentary on the implications of this result — whether it's a leap toward universal quantum computing, or still constrained by hardware limits.

### Research note

- **What was announced:** A Milwaukee Journal Sentinel report published November 11, 2026, described a pilot in which Prolific Arms, the Milwaukee Fire Department and the city’s Office of Community Wellness and Safety planned free gun-lock-box giveaways and installation help at two fire stations on November 21. The report said the city provided a **$6,000 grant** for the pilot. ([aol.com](https://www.aol.com/articles/free-gun-lock-boxes-offered-110250000.html?utm_source=openai))
- **Primary-source check:** Prolific Arms’ event listing advertised the November 21 giveaway at Firehouse 13, with boxes for the first 50 registrants and safety demonstrations. This is evidence of the event plan, not confirmation of how many boxes were handed out. ([stayhappening.com](https://stayhappening.com/e/free-gunlock-box-E2IT036XCSL?utm_source=openai))
- **Did it happen, and was there an improvement?** A November 22 Wisevoter article says the Station 13 event took place and “dozens” of boxes were distributed, but it also says the number distributed was unreported and identifies the Journal Sentinel as its reporting source. I found no independent post-event confirmation or measured evidence that the initiative reduced thefts, injuries or deaths. Treat distribution as **reported but not independently verified**; the claim of a “tangible safety improvement” is not established by the sources located. ([wisevoter.com](https://wisevoter.com/world/us/wi/milwaukee/2026/11/22/milwaukee-groups-give-away-gun-lock-boxes?utm_source=openai))
- **Source overlap:** AOL’s version identifies the November 11 article as originating with the Journal Sentinel; it is a republication, not independent corroboration. ([aol.com](https://www.aol.com/articles/free-gun-lock-boxes-offered-110250000.html?utm_source=openai))

**Bottom line:** The sources support a funded pilot and a planned giveaway; a secondary article reports that boxes were distributed. They do not establish a measured safety outcome.

stories.research_notes:
I found **no credible evidence** to support the event as described in the candidate summary (“Volunteers build 150 bikes for Coweta residents”) with that date (November 22, 2026) or that exact claim. Below is a breakdown of what was and was not found, to clarify what is known and what remains unverified.

---

### What *was* found

1. **Similar bike build events in Coweta County are real**, and are covered by the local media:
   - The *Coweta Sheriff’s Office Big Bike Build* aims to provide **300 bicycles** for children in need during the holidays. ([fox5atlanta.com](https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/coweta-sheriffs-big-bike-build-aims-provide-300-bicycles-kids-need?utm_source=openai))
   - A **GoFundMe fundraiser** aims to pay for 300 bikes via the “CCSO Bike Build Off” event. ([gofundme.com](https://www.gofundme.com/f/the-6th-annual-ccso-bike-build-off?_dt=eyJuYW1lIjoiQy5KLiBE4oCZT25vZnJpbyIsInJvbGUiOiJjbyIsImZ1bmRyYWlzZXJJZCI6IjkyNzIwMjY5In0&modal=profile&utm_source=openai))
   - Bike-Walk Fayette’s “Bikes for Kids” recycling/donation program (for disadvantaged youth/adults in Coweta/Fayette County) has operated for many years. ([bikewalkfayette.org](https://bikewalkfayette.org/donate-a-bike?utm_source=openai))

2. **No confirmation** of “150 bikes built for Coweta residents” in any source that was accessible, including the Newnan Times-Herald, Coweta County outlets, or other regional news media up to the date of this search.

---

### What *was not found / remains unverified*

- No primary or independent source was found confirming the headline: **“Volunteers build 150 bikes for Coweta residents — The Newnan Times-Herald”**.  
- Specifically, no article with the phrase “Volunteers build 150 bikes for Coweta residents” or describing exactly that outcome (number of bikes, volunteer build, residents receiving bikes) was found.
- No verification was found that the event as summarized (150 bikes built, completed and delivered to residents) actually occurred, as opposed to being a plan, pledge, or early-stage announcement.

---

### Conclusion

- The **fact that community bike builds are underway** in Coweta County is well-supported. However, the specific claim that **150 bikes have already been built** and delivered to residents (as of the “date” given) is **not supported by the current evidence**.
- It is possible the summary is conflating or mis-remembering details from other events (e.g. builds with 300 bikes, or fundraising for bike distribution) but no source confirms the summary as stated.

---

If you like, I can try to check restricted content (paywalled) of the Newnan Times-Herald or Coweta local archives to see if the event is reported but not indexed publicly. Would you prefer that?
